page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: What the mixture is
lines: Producer gas is a mixture of carbon
The nitrogen is in it because air is
used to make the gas, and the nitrogen
of the air does not react.
So producer gas always contains a large
volume of nitrogen along with the
steps.why: The nitrogen in producer gas is there only because air was used instead of steam. Saying that in the first step explains the composition rather than asking a student to memorise it.
common_mistakes: Naming the mixture as CO and H₂. That composition is water gas; producer gas has nitrogen in place of the hydrogen.
Leaving the nitrogen out. Nitrogen is the larger part of producer gas and has to be named.
steps.memory_tip: Air was used, so the nitrogen of the air is still there: producer gas is CO plus N₂.
steps.margin_note: Name both gases and say that the nitrogen comes from the air used to make it.

steps.label: The composition and the use

lines.text: Producer gas is used as a cheap fuel

lines: Nitrogen is the largest part of the
mixture and it does not burn.
The carbon monoxide is the part that
burns, so producer gas is used as a low
cost fuel for heating and in furnaces.
steps.why: The rough percentages follow from the way the gas is made: air supplies about four parts of nitrogen for every one part of oxygen, and each oxygen molecule gives two molecules of carbon monoxide, so two volumes of CO come with four of N₂ — about one third and two thirds.
common_mistakes: Writing that the nitrogen burns as well. Nitrogen is non-combustible; only the carbon monoxide burns.
Giving the composition and stopping. One closing line naming the use as a fuel completes the answer.
steps.memory_tip: One oxygen molecule gives two CO, and brings four N₂ with it: 2 parts CO to 4 parts N₂, so one third and two thirds.
steps.margin_note: The percentages are approximate figures for an ordinary sample, so write them as about.

insider_note: Producer gas and water gas are the two that get mixed up. Producer gas is CO with nitrogen; water gas is CO with hydrogen.
